chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from Abī Ayyūb al-Khazzāz, from Sulaymān, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who hired a worker, and he steals from his house: is his hand to be cut off? He said: “This is one entrusted, not a thief; rather, this is a betrayer.”

key_terms.بِسَارِقٍ: not legally classified as a thief in this context
key_terms.تُقْطَعُ يَدُهُ: his hand is cut off; the hadd punishment for theft
key_terms.مُؤْتَمَنٌ: a person entrusted with access or trust

ai.seo_question: Does the hand get cut off if a hired worker steals from his employer’s house?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning an employee who steals from the house of the one who hired him. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام distinguishes between theft and betrayal of trust, ruling that such a person is considered entrusted and treacherous rather than a thief liable to the hadd punishment of hand-cutting.
